questions.stem: A team checks the refund limit in a PostToolUse hook and, when a refund is above the limit, the hook exits with code 2. Large refunds still happen. What is the cause, and the fix?

options.text: Exit 2 does not block in the SDK, so the hook must return a denial
options.says: Ruled out because exit 2 reports back and cannot stop what has run: for `PostToolUse` it "Shows stderr to Claude; the tool already ran".

options.text: Post hooks may not fire at all, so the limit needs a much longer timeout
options.says: Ruled out because the turn-limit case is a different one: "Hooks may not fire when the agent hits the `max_turns` limit because the session ends before hooks can execute".

options.text: The money has already moved by then, so the control belongs ahead of the call
options.says: A post hook runs after the effect.

options.text: The matcher cannot see amounts, so the limit should be written into the matcher
options.says: Ruled out because a matcher carries no limit: "Matchers only match tool names, not file paths or other arguments." The amount is read inside the hook, and the fault is the event: "A control that must prevent an effect therefore belongs in `PreToolUse`".

questions.stem: On Claude Code v2.1.210 or later, a PreToolUse gate in the SDK waits on a slow vendor lookup and exceeds its time limit. What does the model receive, and is the action carried out?

options.text: A normal result, and the operation goes ahead
options.says: Ruled out because the tool is not run: "Claude Code doesn't run the tool call".

options.text: A message that no reply arrived before the deadline, and the operation is withheld
options.says: A timed-out gate is the safe case: nothing runs and the model is told.

options.text: A rejection from a person, and the whole run stops until someone responds to it
options.says: Ruled out because the model gets a result and the turn goes on: "Claude receives a tool result stating the hook didn't respond before its timeout".

options.text: Nothing at all, and the turn simply waits until the gate finally gives its answer
options.says: Ruled out because a callback past its timeout is stopped: "Claude Code cancels it and discards its output".

questions.stem: A second callback was written to use the corrected input that a first callback produces, and it sometimes sees the original. What is the right design?

options.text: Register the second one first so that it always runs before the other
options.says: Ruled out because the order of registration does not set the order of completion: "all matching hooks run in parallel".

options.text: Add a delay to the second one so that the first has time to finish
options.says: Ruled out because a delay guesses at an order that nothing fixes: "completion order is non-deterministic".

options.text: Return the corrected input from both, so that the last one applies
options.says: Ruled out because the callbacks are not ranked: "Two hooks cannot be a pipeline."

options.text: Merge both steps into one function, as handlers finish in any order
